Thanks Jamal - that's very helpful. To give Acme a clear comparison we ran a short target-price benchmark and typical vendor ranges (high-level, per 1M generation tokens):

- OpenAI (managed): $35-$120 / 1M tokens (varies widely by model & context length; premium models and low-latency Gen models sit at the high end).
- Anthropic (managed): $40-$90 / 1M tokens for comparable assistant models.
- Open-model hosts (self-hosted / cloud-hosted with quantization): $8-$30 / 1M tokens depending on instance efficiency, batching, and caching.
- Redwood (hosted, committed tiers): typical target ranges we can deliver are $15-$30 / 1M tokens at the 3-12 month committed volumes, with steeper discounts at larger commits (we can get to low-mid $teens at >1B tokens/year committed).

Notes / tradeoffs:
- The low end of the self-hosted range assumes high engineering effort and optimizations (mixed precision quant, high-batch utilization, aggressive KV caching).
- Managed providers (OpenAI/Anthropic) add convenience and model upgrades but at a premium; hosts that offer open-model variants give better unit economics but require careful kernel/runtime tuning to hold latency SLOs.
- Redwood can offer an introductory committed tier (3-6 months) with a 10-20% introductory discount on the tiered workbook attached, plus an option to reprice at renewal based on observed token mix (short vs long-context generation).

If $20 / 1M tokens is your internal target, we can structure a pilot pricing example that hits that number in a few ways:
1) Blended model: use a mix of a high-efficiency open model for lower-latency flows + a higher-quality model for heavy generations, with caching to reduce billed tokens.
2) Commit + burst: commit to a 6-month minimum volume to get the $/1M target for steady-state; bursts overcommit priced at a slightly higher overage rate.
3) Quantization profile: we can present a quality/cost matrix showing customer-observed output quality vs quantization level (we'll include examples in the workbook).

Next steps I propose:
- I will produce a worked example (3 scenarios) that maps your 50M steady / 150M peak to effective monthly spend and blended $/1M based on model mix.
- Schedule procurement + legal call Thursday 2/18 at 2:30 PM PST (let me know if that works).
- If procurement wants an initial MSA + SOW skeleton, Marissa can start that draft after we lock the numbers.

Are you available for 2/18 2:30 PM PST? If yes I'll lock the invite and send the workbook + scenario notes by end of day.

Best -
Vanessa Ortiz
